vocabularyFiles.src/action-digest.ts: root kernel: string-Keyring CONSUMER, and deliberately not a resolver. It never parses, assembles or narrows a keyring itself — the caller-supplied trust root is handed VERBATIM to verifyChain and to resolveVerificationKey, which is why a lifecycle document and a static map behave here exactly as they do everywhere else, retired-key refusal included. It constructs no KeyEntry (validFrom/revokedAt/roles appear zero times) and reads exactly one field off a resolved result: publicKey, to verify the execution grant's §6 signature. Grant ROLE/expiry semantics are verifyArtifact's and are documented as a residual in docs/action-digest-spec.md §6 rather than approximated here.

vocabularyFiles.packages/relay/test/adr0007-e2e-http.tes: ADR-0007 end-to-end HTTP test: publicKeyHex is the raw key a phone PRESENTS over the wire; this file builds no KeyEntry and resolves no keyring — it drives the real routes and asserts their refusals
vocabularyFiles.packages/gate/src/grant-sidecar.ts: out-of-process grant signer: CONSUMES an operator-provisioned keyring and receiptKeyring wholesale (loadGrantSignerTrust passes the parsed object straight to verifyArtifact/verifyChain, selects no fields and synthesises none), so the P0-1/P0-5/P0-8 dropped-validFrom class is not expressible here — there is no per-entry construction to drop it in

EX-TEST-FIXTURES.reason: Test/vector/fixture keyrings legitimately pin absent, legacy and malformed states — several exist precisely to prove the legacy always-active rule and the fail-closed malformed rule. They stay fully censused: a NEW test resolver still fails the gate until inventoried.

EX-EVID-TERSE-ROOT.reason: The terse tenant-root form (kid -> SPKI string) has nowhere to declare temporal fields; entries are always-active by the documented P0-1 compatibility rule ('absent stays absent, no default invented'). The full-object form (ordinal 1) carries both fields.

EX-DELEGATION-NO-REVOCATION.reason: noa.key-delegation/0.1 declares validFrom + expiresAt and has NO revocation field, so there is no declared revokedAt to carry; the DELEGATED entry's revokedAt is absent because the wire format cannot express it. Lifecycle bounding is the delegation's own expiresAt, verified on the delegation artifact. If 0.2 adds delegation revocation this exception must be deleted and carriage added.

EX-RELAY-DEVICE.reason: Relay DeviceRecords (publicKeyHex) are enrolment credentials in the relay's rootless registry, not KeyEntry trust anchors: the gate re-verifies every decision against its OWN keyring and never trusts relay device state. Activation is not modeled on device credentials; revocation exists (revokedAt via revokeSelf) and is covered by the relay suite.

EX-STRING-KEYRING.reason: An explicitly supplied static Keyring (kid -> base64 SPKI) is the compatibility shape for non-rotating consumers and structurally carries no lifecycle assertion. In-repo resolvers must not manufacture it from lifecycle data: rotating trust uses SigningKeyLifecycle, preserves revocation as retiredAt, and refuses every non-null retirement outright. validFrom remains a KeyEntry-side activation rule and is not represented by the receipt lifecycle schema.
